findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks all custom grant-type factories
findings.body: getShortcut() was added as an abstract interface method with no default implementation. Every existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory outside this PR (and any test/deployment extension implementing the old interface) will fail to compile, and already-compiled implementations will throw AbstractMethodError when the encoder factory calls getShortcut() during postInit or token issuance. A default method (e.g. returning the unknown shortcut) is needed to preserve SPI compatibility.

findings.title: Public copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context was removed
findings.body: The public Context(Context) copy constructor was deleted and replaced by initialization of grantType from formParams. Code that copied a grant context (custom grants, token-exchange flows, tests) no longer compiles. In addition, grantType is now captured once from formParams at construction, so a later setFormParams() call silently leaves getGrantType() returning the stale original value, which is then encoded into the access-token ID.

findings.title: Token issuance now fails for any unregistered grant type
findings.body: encodeTokenId() throws IllegalStateException whenever getShortcutByGrantType() returns null, and TokenManager.initToken() now calls this for every access token. Previously token creation never depended on the grant type being known to this registry. Any flow that sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE to a value without a registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory with that exact ID (custom grants, non-grant issuance paths that propagate a grant string, or a grant whose factory is feature-disabled and absent from the session factory) will now fail token creation entirely instead of issuing a token with an unknown-context ID.

findings.title: Shortcut length/uniqueness contract is not validated but decoder assumes exactly 2 chars
findings.body: postInit() registers whatever getShortcut() returns without checking it is non-null and exactly 2 characters, and the interface javadoc even suggests 'usually like 3-letters'. encodeTokenId() simply concatenates the shortcut, so a 1- or 3-character (or null) shortcut produces a token ID whose prefix is not 6 characters (or an NPE from ConcurrentHashMap.put for null), and getTokenContextFromTokenId() will then reject every such token with IllegalArgumentException. The factory only checks duplicate map sizes, not the format the wire encoding depends on.

findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: Line 72 checks grantType and line 73 checks grantType again with the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed'; rawTokenId itself is never null-checked. A null rawTokenId therefore passes construction and later produces a token ID ending in ':null' from encodeTokenId(), or corrupt data returned from getRawTokenId(), instead of failing fast at the point of the programming error.

findings.title: Decoder throws on any colon-containing token ID that is not in the new format
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId() returns UNKNOWN only when the ID contains no ':' at all; any other ID containing a colon but with a prefix that is not exactly 6 known characters throws IllegalArgumentException. Token IDs are attacker/client-influenced input (jti of presented tokens) and older or externally/custom-generated IDs may legitimately contain colons. Future consumers using this decoder for introspection/userinfo/session lookup (the stated purpose of the PR) will turn such tokens into 500 errors instead of treating the context as unknown like pre-upgrade UUID tokens.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring offset
findings.body: The encoded prefix is session(0-1)+tokenType(2-3)+grant(4-5), but the matcher checks substring(3,5), and returns false when that substring equals the expected grant shortcut instead of when it differs. As written it rejects (partly) matching IDs for the wrong reason and accepts IDs whose grant shortcut is wrong, so expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken do not actually verify the grant-type encoding this PR introduces. It should check substring(4,6) and return false on inequality.
